pass_a_gloss:
The tongue speaks like the hand does good. Another is the voice of words, another the smell of accomplishments. The former is heavy in the air, the latter reaches heaven and fulfills the ones above, the latter stands by the ones above. Time will leave me while narrating, says Paul. If time left Paul while speaking of the accomplishments of the saints, Paul in whom Christ spoke, in whom the fullness of the church reached, an inexhaustible treasure of knowledge was hidden - a metal of knowledge, searching the law and the prophets from above, having a tongue in the whole world like a trumpet in a theater - what shall we do, we poor and needy? What shall we do, we who are untaught in word, weak in tongue, slow in mind and uneducated in heart, who have not learned external knowledge nor exercised internal knowledge? There is no citizenship that draws boldness, nor life that speaks instead of word. From where shall we weave a garment of praises for Anthony? Now let David's lyre crown him. For about him, in a chapter of a book, and of his holy deeds, it is written: 'Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, in His will he will be very strong. His seed will be powerful on earth.' For his seed is the monastic communities everywhere in Egypt, and more so, everywhere on earth. They consider him a father and a farmer, they regulate their lives according to his examples, and they think he is present through the keeping of the laws. One word from those educated in succession, being saved, is able to establish a citizenship from philosophy.

Let Isaiah the prophet speak about him; blessed is he who has seed in Zion and household in Jerusalem. Let it be said about Antony and these words of Jeremiah's prophecy; before I formed you in the womb, I knew you and before you came out of the womb…
pass_b_english: The tongue speaks like the hand does good.
The voice of words is heavy in the air, while accomplishments reach heaven and fulfill those above, standing by their side.
Even Paul, who spoke on behalf of Christ, found that time was running out as he narrated the accomplishments of the saints, saying, 'Time will leave me while narrating.'
If time was limited for Paul, who had an inexhaustible treasure of knowledge and spoke with the fullness of the church, what can we, who are poor and needy, do to express ourselves?
We, who are untaught in words, weak in tongue, slow in mind, and uneducated in heart, have not learned external knowledge nor exercised internal knowledge.
There is no external factor that can give us the boldness to speak, nor can our life experiences replace the need for words.
The challenge lies in finding the right words to praise Anthony.
Now, let the music of David's lyre be the crown that honors him.
As it is written, 'Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, in His will he will be very strong. His seed will be powerful on earth' (Psalm 112:1).
For Anthony, his seed refers to the monastic communities that have sprouted everywhere in Egypt and around the world.
These communities consider him a father and a role model, regulating their lives according to his examples and keeping his laws.
Even a single word from those who are educated in the ways of philosophy can establish a sense of citizenship and belonging.
Let the prophet Isaiah speak about Anthony, saying, 'Blessed is he who has seed in Zion and a household in Jerusalem' (Isaiah 32:17).
And as Jeremiah's prophecy says, 'Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you and before you came out of the womb' (Jeremiah 1:5).
